reading.title: One Meaning, Four Spellings
reading.purpose: Find out why four prefixes all mean not and how the first letter of a word picks the right one.
paras: English has a small puzzle: four different prefixes, in-, im-, il-, and ir-, all mean not. Why so many? The answer is sound. A prefix changes its shape so that the whole word is easier to say.
Before most letters, the prefix stays in-. If a supply of water is not adequate, it is inadequate. A schedule that keeps changing from week to week is inconsistent.

Before the letters m, b, and p, the prefix becomes im-. An immature plant has not finished growing. An impractical plan sounds nice but cannot work in real life. A feeling too great to count, such as thanks for a rescue, is immeasurable.

Before l, the prefix becomes il-. Handwriting so messy that no one can read it is illegible, and an argument that does not make sense is illogical. Before r, the prefix becomes ir-. A comment with no connection to the topic is irrelevant, a rare family photograph that no one could swap for another is irreplaceable, and a person who ignores duties is irresponsible.

Notice the pattern: the spelling follows the first letter of the base word. If you want to say that a rule is not regular, you write irregular, not inregular. Be careful, though, because in- sometimes means inside, as in the word inhale. When you meet a long word that begins with il-, im-, in-, or ir-, test it by removing the prefix and asking whether the rest of the word makes sense.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, the word "immature" describes something that
choices: cannot work when people try it in real life
is too great for anyone to count or measure
has no real connection to the topic at hand
qs.why: The example says an immature plant "has not finished growing."

qs.q: Which sentence names two words that begin with il-?
choices: Before l, the prefix becomes il-.
A comment with no connection to the topic is irrelevant, a rare family photograph that no one could swap for another is irreplaceable, and a person who ignores duties is irresponsible.
Handwriting so messy that no one can read it is illegible, and an argument that does not make sense is illogical.
Before r, the prefix becomes ir-.
qs.why: Illegible and illogical both begin with il-, and this is the only sentence that names both.

ev.text: Handwriting so messy that no one can read it is illegible, and an argument that does not make sense is illogical.

qs.q: Why does the writer say to write irregular, not inregular?
choices: The prefix changes to fit the next letter.
The word irregular was invented before the word regular.
The prefix ir- is used only for words about rules and laws.
Words that begin with in- are never spelled correctly.
qs.why: The writer's pattern is that the prefix's spelling follows the first letter of the base word, and regular begins with r.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Every word that begins with in- must have a negative meaning.
Most long English words come from the same few base words.
A prefix should never be removed from the front of a word.
Spelling shifts so that one meaning has four prefixes.
qs.why: The reading explains that in-, im-, il-, and ir- all mean not and change shape to fit the next sound.

clues.text: sounds nice but cannot work in real life
so messy that no one can read it
